articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of promoting the development of the museum industry, giving full play to the functions of museums, meeting the spiritual and cultural needs of citizens, and improving their ideological, moral, scientific and cultural qualities.

Article 2 For the purposes of these Regulations, a museum means a non-profit organization that collects, protects and displays to the public the evidence of human activities and the natural environment for the purposes of education, research and appreciation, and is registered with the registration authority according to law.
Museums include state-owned museums and non-state-owned museums. A museum established with or mainly with state-owned assets is a state-owned museum; a museum established with or mainly with non-state-owned assets is a non-state-owned museum.
The State shall treat state-owned museums and non-state-owned museums equally in terms of the conditions for the establishment of museums, provision of social services, standardized management, evaluation of professional technical titles, financial and tax support policies, among others.

Article 3 Museums shall, in providing social services, adhere to the direction of serving the people and serving socialism, and the principle of keeping close to reality, life and the masses, so as to enrich the spiritual and cultural life of the people.

Article 4 The State shall formulate plans for the development of the museum industry and improve the museum system.
The State encourages enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, citizens and other social forces to establish museums according to law.

Article 5 The operating expenses of state-owned museums shall be included in the fiscal budget at the corresponding level; the sponsors of non-state-owned museums shall ensure the operating expenses of the museums.
The State encourages the establishment of public welfare funds to provide funds for museums, and encourages museums to raise funds through multiple channels to promote their own development.

Article 6 Museums shall enjoy tax benefits according to law.
Those who establish museums according to law or make donations to museums shall enjoy tax benefits in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 7 The competent department of cultural relics under the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of museums nationwide. The other relevant departments of the State Council shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the management of museums.
The competent departments of cultural relics of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of museums within their respective administrative regions. The other relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the management of museums within their respective administrative regions.

Article 8 Museum industry organizations shall, according to law, formulate self-regulation norms, safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of their members, guide and supervise the business activities of their members, and promote the healthy development of the museum industry.
Article 9 Organizations or individuals that have made outstanding contributions to the museum industry shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 12 The establishment, modification, or termination of a state-owned museum shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the relevant laws and administrative regulations on the registration and management of public institutions, and shall be recorded with the cultural relics administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the museum is located.

Article 13 For a museum whose collections include paleontological fossils, its establishment, modification, or termination shall comply with the provisions of the relevant laws and administrative regulations on the protection of paleontological fossils, and shall be recorded with the cultural relics administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the museum is located.

Article 15 For the establishment of a non-state-owned museum whose collections do not include paleontological fossils, the procedures for legal person registration shall be handled with the relevant registration and management authority according to law.
Where a non-state-owned museum as specified in the preceding paragraph undergoes modification or termination, it shall undergo modification registration or cancellation registration with the relevant registration and management authority according to law, and shall record the matter with the cultural relics administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the museum is located.

Article 16 The cultural relics administrative department of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall promptly publish the names, addresses, contact information, main collections, and other information of the museums that have been recorded within its administrative region.
Article 17 A museum shall improve its corporate governance structure and establish and improve the relevant organizational management system.
Article 18 Professional and technical personnel of a museum shall have their professional technical titles assessed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 19 No organization or individual may occupy the assets managed and used by a museum according to law.
A museum may not engage in commercial business activities involving cultural relics or other collections. Where a museum engages in other commercial business activities, it shall not violate the purpose of the museum or harm the interests of visitors. The specific measures for a museum to engage in other commercial business activities shall be formulated by the State cultural relics administrative department.

Article 20 Where a museum accepts donations, it shall comply with the provisions of the relevant laws and administrative regulations.
A museum may, according to law, name its premises or other facilities after the name of its sponsor or donor; a non-state-owned museum may also, according to law, use the name of its sponsor or donor as the name of the museum.

Article 21 Museums may acquire collections through purchase, acceptance of donations, lawful exchange, or other methods as prescribed by laws and administrative regulations, and shall not acquire collections of unknown or illegal origin.

Article 22 Museums shall establish collection accounts and archives. Where a collection is a cultural relic, it shall distinguish the grade of the cultural relic, set up separate cultural relic archives, establish a strict management system, and report to the competent department of cultural relics for recordation.
Collections that have not been accounted or archived in accordance with the preceding paragraph shall not be exchanged or lent out.

Article 23 The legal representative of a museum shall be responsible for the safety of the collections.
Before the departure of the museum's legal representative or collection management personnel, they shall complete the transfer procedures for the collections.

Article 24 Museums shall strengthen the safety management of collections, regularly inspect and maintain the equipment and facilities for ensuring the safety of collections, and ensure their normal operation. Precious collections and fragile collections shall be stored in special warehouses or with special equipment, and shall be kept by specially assigned personnel.

Article 25 Where museum collections are state-owned cultural relics, precious cultural relics among non-state-owned cultural relics, or other cultural relics whose export is prohibited by state regulations, they shall not be exported, and shall not be transferred, leased, or pledged to foreigners.
Where collections of state-owned museums are cultural relics, they shall not be donated, leased, or sold to other entities or individuals.

Article 26 Where a museum terminates, it shall dispose of the collections in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on non-profit organizations; where the collections are cultural relics the sale of which is prohibited by the state, they shall be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on cultural relic protection.

Article 27 Where museum collections are cultural relics or paleontological fossils, their acquisition, protection, management, exhibition, disposal, entry and exit, etc., shall also comply with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on cultural relic protection and paleontological fossil protection respectively.
Article 28 Museums shall open to the public within six months from the date of obtaining the registration certificate.
Article 29 Museums shall announce the specific opening hours to the public. During statutory holidays and winter and summer vacations of schools, museums shall be open.

Article 31 Where a museum holds an exhibition, it shall, 10 working days before the start date of the exhibition, file the exhibition theme, exhibit descriptions, commentary scripts, etc. with the competent cultural relics department or other relevant departments of the place where the exhibition is held.
The competent cultural relics departments of the people's governments at all levels and museum industry organizations shall strengthen guidance and supervision over museum exhibitions.

Article 32 Museums shall assign appropriate professional personnel to provide explanations based on the comprehension abilities of minors of different age groups. During school winter and summer vacations, museums with appropriate conditions shall add exhibition items suitable for students' characteristics.

Article 33 The State encourages museums to be open to the public free of charge. The people's governments at or above the county level shall provide necessary financial support to museums that are open to the public free of charge.
Where a museum is not open free of charge, its ticket prices, charged items and standards shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, and shall be published at a conspicuous place at the charging point.
Where a museum is not open free of charge, it shall provide free admission or other concessions to minors, adult students, teachers, elderly persons, disabled persons, military personnel, etc. The items and standards for concessions provided by the museum shall be announced to the public.

Article 34 Museums shall, based on their own characteristics and conditions, use modern information technology to carry out various forms of lively social education and service activities, and participate in community cultural development and foreign cultural exchanges and cooperation.
The State encourages museums to explore the connotation of collections, integrate with cultural creativity, tourism and other industries, develop derivative products, and enhance the museums' development capacity.

Article 35 The education administrative department of the State Council shall, together with the national competent cultural relics department, formulate policies and measures for using museum resources to carry out education, teaching and social practice activities.
The education administrative departments of the local people's governments at all levels shall encourage schools to organize students to carry out study and practice activities in museums in conjunction with curriculum settings and teaching plans.
Museums shall provide support and assistance to schools in carrying out various relevant education and teaching activities.

Article 36 Museums shall give full play to the advantages of collections, conduct theoretical and applied research in relevant professional fields, improve professional standards, and promote the growth of professional talents.
Museums shall provide support and assistance to institutions of higher learning, scientific research institutions, experts and scholars, etc. in carrying out scientific research work.
Article 37 The public shall take care of museum exhibits, facilities and the environment, and shall not damage museum exhibits or facilities.

Article 38 Museum industry organizations may evaluate museums based on their education, service, collection protection, research and exhibition levels. Specific measures shall be formulated by the national competent cultural relics department together with other relevant departments.

Article 39 Where a museum acquires collections of unknown or illegal origin, or the theme or content of an exhibition causes adverse effects, the competent cultural relics department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, or the relevant registration administration authority, shall, according to their respective functions and duties, order correction, if there are illegal gains, confiscate the illegal gains and impose a fine of not less than 2 times but not more than 5 times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains, impose a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the registration administration authority shall revoke the registration.

Article 40 Where a museum engages in commercial business activities involving cultural relics collections, the administrative department for industry and commerce shall impose penalties in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations on cultural relics protection.
Where a museum engages in commercial business activities involving non-cultural relics collections, or engages in other commercial business activities that violate the purpose of the museum and harm the interests of visitors, the competent cultural relics department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, or the relevant registration administration authority, shall, according to their respective functions and duties, order correction, if there are illegal gains, confiscate the illegal gains and impose a fine of not less than 2 times but not more than 5 times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains, impose a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the registration administration authority shall revoke the registration.

Article 41 If a museum fails to open to the public within six months from the date of obtaining the registration certificate, or fails to implement free admission or other preferential measures in accordance with these Regulations, the cultural relics administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall order it to make corrections; if it refuses to make corrections, the registration authority shall revoke the registration.

Article 42 Where a museum violates the provisions of relevant price laws or administrative regulations, the competent pricing department of the local people's government at or above the county level where the museum is located shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 43 Where the cultural relics administrative department or any other relevant department of the people's government at or above the county level, or any of their staff members, neglects duties, abuses power, engages in malpractices for personal gain, or takes advantage of the position to extort or accept property from others, the people's government at the same level or the competent authority at a higher level shall order correction and circulate a notice of criticism; the person directly in charge and other directly liable persons shall be given sanctions according to law.
Article 44 Any violation of these Regulations that constitutes a crime shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.
Article 45 For the purposes of these Regulations, a museum does not include science popularization venues intended for popularizing science and technology.
Article 46 The museums under the Chinese People's Liberation Army shall be managed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the armed forces.
Article 47 These Regulations shall come into force as of March 20, 2015.
